headline: Medium risk: dbt-core can egress warehouse data while LlamaFactory has no file/network surfaces, so leakage and conflict are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default injection bridge is documented. dbt-core exposes only allowlisted network egress and warehouse API calls, while LlamaFactory has no clipboard, filesystem, stdin/stdout, browser, or MCP surfaces. Without a shared channel, prompt injection between them is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies dbt-core output into LlamaFactory prompts, the risk becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is added later, re-evaluate for injection bridging.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared prompt channel.
Do not pipe dbt-core logs into LlamaFactory inputs.
Disable any future clipboard or file-based handoff between them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags if a shared orchestrator is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and can egress to allowlisted network destinations, so sensitive warehouse content may leave its local boundary. LlamaFactory currently shows no file read, stdin/stdout, or network egress, so it is not the main leak path. The pair still creates a medium leakage risk because dbt-core can expose sensitive data through its normal workflow.
conditions: IF dbt-core is pointed at sensitive warehouse tables, leakage impact increases.
IF LlamaFactory is later given file or network access, the pairwise leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Restrict dbt-core to non-sensitive schemas.
Review allowlisted egress destinations for dbt-core.
Keep LlamaFactory offline and without file access.
Mask or exclude sensitive columns before dbt runs.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on warehouse exports.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is documented. dbt-core has warehouse API access and allowlisted egress, but no filesystem write or git mutation is listed; LlamaFactory explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. The profiles do not show a shared mutable resource, so capability conflict is not plausible here.
conditions: IF dbt-core is deployed with additional filesystem or git write permissions, conflict risk must be re-evaluated.
IF both agents are later granted access to the same mutable workspace, conflict becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep dbt-core away from shared git worktrees.
Do not grant LlamaFactory write permissions.
Separate warehouse credentials from any local workspace credentials.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading error path is weakly present because dbt-core can produce warehouse-derived outputs that another system might treat as authoritative, but LlamaFactory has no documented action-taking or ingestion path. Since the pair lacks a direct handoff mechanism, the blast radius is small and the pathway requires extra orchestration not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an external workflow feeds dbt-core outputs into LlamaFactory prompts, cascading errors become more plausible.
IF LlamaFactory is wrapped in an action-taking orchestrator, downstream impact increases.
mitigations: Require human review of dbt outputs before reuse.
Do not auto-ingest dbt artifacts into LlamaFactory.
Label dbt outputs as untrusted data, not facts.
requires-engineering: add validation checks before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: Only dbt-core is clearly tied to a regulated data class: data warehouse data. LlamaFactory shows no touched data classes or residency/compliance claims, so there is no documented mismatch. The remaining concern is limited to ordinary handling of warehouse data by dbt-core, which is a low compliance risk absent a second regulated surface.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated records, compliance review is required.
IF LlamaFactory later processes the same regulated data class, reassess residency and retention.
mitigations: Classify warehouse datasets before dbt runs.
Avoid sending regulated records into any downstream LlamaFactory workflow.
Document retention for dbt artifacts.
requires-engineering: add residency controls if regulated data is introduced.
